title: A CPU Made of Atoms: IBM's Breakthrough 0.7nm Transistors
gist: A short SemiWiki post promoting a video walkthrough of IBM's 7A Nanostack architecture, which stacks NMOS and PMOS transistors vertically in a complementary FET (CFET) configuration. The framing is a disagreement among industry players over whether Moore's Law scaling still works: IBM says yes, Nvidia says scaling is dead, TSMC is indifferent.

insights.claim: IBM's 7A Nanostack architecture stacks an NMOS and a PMOS transistor vertically on top of each other, an approach the industry calls a complementary FET or CFET.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: CFET is the presumed post-GAA device architecture; an IBM research demonstration signals where foundry capex and EDA tool investment go next.
insights.quote: how IBM stacks an NMOS and a PMOS transistor on top of each other in what the industry calls a complementary FET, or CFET
insights.locator: In this video I go through what 7A Nanostack is

insights.claim: The transistor scaling roadmap has progressed from planar to FinFET to gate-all-around, with vertical NMOS/PMOS stacking as the next step beyond gate-all-around.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A clean mental model for staging equipment and materials demand — each architecture transition reprices the process-tool and metrology suppliers.
insights.quote: the shift from planar to FinFET to gate-all-around
insights.locator: We start with the basics of a transistor

insights.claim: IBM positions the 7A Nanostack explicitly as proof that Moore's Law is not finished.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If density scaling continues, the cost-per-transistor curve that underwrites AI compute economics stays intact rather than flattening.
insights.quote: IBM reckons Moore's Law isn't finished, and their new 7A Nanostack is how they're proving it.
insights.locator: IBM reckons Moore's Law isn't finished

themes.theme: Industry split on whether scaling is dead

insights.claim: Nvidia publicly maintains that transistor scaling is dead, while IBM argues scaling still works — the two leading voices on the roadmap are in direct opposition.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The 'scaling is dead' narrative is what justifies Nvidia's system-level and packaging premium; a working CFET path partially undercuts that justification.
insights.quote: Ask Nvidia and they'll tell you scaling is dead. Ask TSMC and they don't seem to care either way. IBM lands firmly on yes, scaling still works.
insights.locator: Ask Nvidia and they'll tell you scaling is dead

insights.claim: TSMC is described as indifferent to the scaling-is-dead debate, neither endorsing nor rejecting it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The dominant foundry's agnosticism suggests it wins on either path — a reason its position is more defensible than either device-architecture bet.
insights.quote: Ask TSMC and they don't seem to care either way.
insights.locator: Ask Nvidia and they'll tell you scaling is dead

insights.claim: The 7A Nanostack claims trace to peer-reviewed VLSI conference papers — Reboh et al. on NanoStack transistor architecture for the CMOS 7A node at VLSI 2025 and Zhang et al. on staggered-channel Nanostack SRAM bitcells at VLSI 2026 — plus an IBM newsroom announcement dated June 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: SRAM bitcell papers are the tell for whether a device architecture is manufacturable at density, not just demonstrable — that is where scaling usually stalls.
insights.quote: Zhang et al, Area and Performance of Staggered-Channel Nanostack SRAM Bitcells, VLSI 2026

insights.claim: More Than Moore discloses that it provides or has provided paid research, analysis, advising or consulting to a long list of industry participants including IBM, Nvidia, Intel, TSMC and Synopsys — the same firms whose roadmap positions the piece characterizes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Read the IBM-favorable framing with the disclosure in mind — analyst-firm coverage of device roadmaps is not independent by default.
insights.quote: More Than Moore, as with other research and analyst firms, provides or has provided paid research, analysis, advising, or consulting to many high-tech companies in the industry
insights.locator: More Than Moore, as with other research
